original_query: When should an antimalarial medicine recommended in a national treatment policy be changed due to treatment failure?
normalized_query: when to change recommended antimalarial medicine in national malaria treatment policy total treatment failure proportion threshold
gold_answer: An antimalarial medicine should be changed if the total treatment failure proportion is ≥ 10%, as assessed in vivo by monitoring therapeutic efficacy.
gold_claims: An antimalarial medicine recommended in national policy should be changed if the total treatment failure proportion is ≥ 10% in vivo.

original_query: What average cure rate in clinical trials is required to introduce a new antimalarial medicine into national treatment policy?
normalized_query: average cure rate clinical trials required to introduce new antimalarial medicine national treatment policy
gold_answer: An average cure rate of > 95% as assessed in clinical trials.
gold_claims: Introducing a new antimalarial medicine into national treatment policy requires an average cure rate of > 95% in clinical trials.

original_query: What formulation of paediatric antimalarial drugs is preferred for young children and infants?
normalized_query: preferred paediatric antimalarial formulations for young children and infants solid vs liquid dispersible tablets
gold_answer: Solid formulations (e.g. dispersible tablets) are preferred over liquid formulations.
gold_claims: Solid paediatric formulations such as dispersible tablets are preferred over liquid formulations for young children and infants.

original_query: Is mass testing and treatment (MTaT) recommended to reduce malaria transmission?
normalized_query: is mass testing and treatment MTaT recommended to reduce malaria transmission WHO guidance
gold_answer: Mass testing and treatment (MTaT) to reduce the transmission of malaria is not recommended.
gold_claims: Mass testing and treatment (MTaT) to reduce malaria transmission is not recommended.

original_query: Who can receive targeted drug administration (TDA) as chemoprevention in very low to low transmission settings?
normalized_query: target population for targeted drug administration TDA chemoprevention low transmission settings
gold_answer: People with increased risk of infection relative to the general population.
gold_claims: Targeted drug administration can be given to individuals with an increased risk of infection compared to the general population.

original_query: Is routine malaria testing and treatment recommended for individuals arriving at points of entry?
normalized_query: is routine malaria testing and treatment at points of entry land sea air recommended to reduce importation
gold_answer: Routine malaria testing and treatment of people arriving at points of entry (land, sea or air) to reduce importation is not recommended.
gold_claims: Routine malaria testing and treatment at points of entry to reduce importation is not recommended.

original_query: Who should be given antimalarial medicine as chemoprevention in reactive drug administration (RDA)?
normalized_query: target population for reactive drug administration RDA chemoprevention confirmed malaria case contacts
gold_answer: All people residing with or near a confirmed malaria case and all people who share the same risk of infection (e.g. co-travellers and co-workers).
gold_claims: Reactive drug administration is provided to individuals living with or near a confirmed case, as well as those sharing the same infection risk such as co-workers and co-travellers.

original_query: Where should reactive indoor residual spraying (IRS) be conducted following a confirmed malaria case?
normalized_query: where to conduct reactive indoor residual spraying IRS confirmed malaria cases houses neighbours
gold_answer: In the houses of confirmed cases and neighbours.
gold_claims: Reactive indoor residual spraying of insecticide can be conducted in the houses of confirmed cases and their neighbours.

original_query: What does the medical abbreviation AL stand for in the WHO malaria guidelines?
normalized_query: medical abbreviation AL meaning artemether lumefantrine WHO malaria guidelines
gold_answer: artemether-lumefantrine
gold_claims: AL stands for artemether-lumefantrine.

original_query: What does the abbreviation IPTp stand for?
normalized_query: abbreviation IPTp full form intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy
gold_answer: intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy
gold_claims: IPTp stands for intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy.

original_query: What is the full meaning of the abbreviation SMC in malaria interventions?
normalized_query: abbreviation SMC meaning seasonal malaria chemoprevention
gold_answer: seasonal malaria chemoprevention
gold_claims: SMC stands for seasonal malaria chemoprevention.

original_query: How many estimated global cases and deaths from malaria occurred in 2023 according to the World malaria report?
normalized_query: estimated global malaria cases and deaths 2023 World malaria report
gold_answer: An estimated 263 million cases and 597 000 malaria deaths globally in 2023.
gold_claims: In 2023, there were an estimated 263 million cases and 597,000 deaths from malaria globally.

original_query: What is the 2030 Global Technical Strategy target for reducing malaria mortality rates compared to 2015?
normalized_query: Global Technical Strategy 2030 target percentage reduction malaria mortality rates compared to 2015
gold_answer: At least 90%
gold_claims: The target for reducing global malaria mortality rates by 2030 compared with 2015 is at least 90%.

original_query: How many countries is the Global Technical Strategy targeting for malaria elimination by 2025?
normalized_query: GTS 2025 target number of countries to eliminate malaria transmitted in 2015
gold_answer: At least 20 countries
gold_claims: The target for 2025 is to eliminate malaria from at least 20 countries in which malaria was transmitted in 2015.

original_query: Which Plasmodium species commonly infect humans, and which is considered the most dangerous?
normalized_query: Plasmodium species infecting humans P. falciparum P. vivax P. malariae P. ovale most dangerous species
gold_answer: The four species that most commonly infect humans are Plasmodium falciparum, P. vivax, P. malariae, and P. ovale. P. falciparum is the most dangerous.
gold_claims: Plasmodium falciparum, P. vivax, P. malariae, and P. ovale most commonly infect humans.
Plasmodium falciparum is the most dangerous species.

original_query: How long does the malaria parasite typically take to develop inside a mosquito into an infective form for humans?
normalized_query: development time period of malaria parasite inside mosquito to become infective to humans
gold_answer: A period of 7–10 days.
gold_claims: The malaria parasite generally requires 7 to 10 days to develop inside the mosquito into a form infective to humans.

original_query: What annual parasite incidence and P. falciparum prevalence define high malaria transmission areas?
normalized_query: annual parasite incidence API and P falciparum prevalence rate definition for high transmission areas
gold_answer: An annual parasite incidence of 450 or more cases per 1000 population and a P. falciparum prevalence rate of ≥35%.
gold_claims: High transmission areas have an annual parasite incidence of ≥ 450 cases per 1000 population.
High transmission areas have a Plasmodium falciparum prevalence rate of ≥ 35%.

original_query: What is the annual parasite incidence range for areas categorized as having low malaria transmission?
normalized_query: annual parasite incidence range API for low malaria transmission areas per 1000 population
gold_answer: An annual parasite incidence of 100–250 cases per 1000 population.
gold_claims: Low transmission areas have an annual parasite incidence of 100–250 cases per 1000 population.

original_query: Which two vector control interventions are recommended by WHO for large-scale deployment?
normalized_query: malaria vector control interventions recommended for large scale deployment WHO guidelines
gold_answer: Insecticide-treated nets (ITNs) prequalified by WHO and indoor residual spraying (IRS) with a product prequalified by WHO.
gold_claims: WHO-prequalified ITNs and WHO-prequalified indoor residual spraying (IRS) are the vector control interventions recommended for large-scale deployment.

original_query: Approximately how many Anopheles species are major vector species for malaria?
normalized_query: number of Anopheles mosquito species that are major malaria vectors
gold_answer: Around 40 species.
gold_claims: Out of more than 400 Anopheles species, around 40 are major malaria vectors.

original_query: What factors attract female Anopheles mosquitoes to a human host?
normalized_query: factors attracting female Anopheles mosquitoes to human host blood meal
gold_answer: Exhaled carbon dioxide, lactic acid, host odours, warmth, and moisture.
gold_claims: Female mosquitoes are attracted to hosts by exhaled carbon dioxide, lactic acid, host odours, warmth, and moisture.

original_query: What percentage of clinical cases averted in Africa between 2000 and 2015 was attributed to ITNs?
normalized_query: percentage of clinical malaria cases averted in Africa by ITNs between 2000 and 2015
gold_answer: 68% of cases averted.
gold_claims: Insecticide-treated nets (ITNs) made the largest contribution by averting 68% of clinical malaria cases in Africa between 2000 and 2015.

original_query: What percentage of reporting malaria-endemic sites detected pyrethroid resistance in at least one vector species?
normalized_query: percentage of global sites detecting pyrethroid resistance in malaria vectors
gold_answer: 68% of the sites for which data were available.
gold_claims: Globally, resistance to pyrethroids was detected in at least one malaria vector in 68% of monitored sites.

original_query: Why should vector control programmes avoid switching between different pyrethroid insecticides to manage resistance?
normalized_query: switching between pyrethroid insecticides to manage resistance effectiveness WHO guidance
gold_answer: Differences between adult mosquito mortalities in pyrethroid resistance assays are not indicative of a true or operationally relevant difference in performance among commonly used pyrethroids.
gold_claims: Differences in adult mosquito mortality assays do not reflect operationally relevant performance differences among commonly used pyrethroids.

original_query: What are insecticide mixtures in vector control?
normalized_query: definition of insecticide mixtures in malaria vector control
gold_answer: Co-formulations that combine two or more insecticides with different modes of action.
gold_claims: Mixtures are co-formulations combining two or more insecticides with different modes of action.

original_query: How is residual malaria transmission defined?
normalized_query: definition of residual malaria transmission WHO guidelines
gold_answer: The persistence of malaria transmission following the implementation in time and space of a widely effective malaria programme.
gold_claims: Residual transmission refers to ongoing malaria transmission that persists despite the wide implementation of an effective malaria programme.

original_query: How should old insecticide-treated nets be disposed of according to WHO guidelines?
normalized_query: WHO recommended disposal method for old insecticide treated nets ITNs
gold_answer: Old nets should be buried, preferably in non-permeable soil and away from water sources, rather than burned in the open air.
gold_claims: WHO recommends burying old nets in non-permeable soil away from water sources instead of open-air burning.

original_query: By what rate ratio do ITNs reduce all-cause child mortality compared to no nets?
normalized_query: rate ratio reduction all cause child mortality ITNs vs no nets
gold_claims: ITNs reduce all-cause child mortality with a rate ratio of 0.83 compared to no nets.

original_query: How does piperonyl butoxide (PBO) work in pyrethroid-PBO nets to enhance efficacy against resistant mosquitoes?
normalized_query: mechanism of action piperonyl butoxide PBO in pyrethroid PBO ITNs oxidase inhibition
gold_answer: PBO acts by inhibiting certain metabolic enzymes, primarily oxidases, within the mosquito that would otherwise detoxify or sequester pyrethroid insecticides.
gold_claims: Piperonyl butoxide (PBO) inhibits metabolic enzymes, primarily oxidases, preventing mosquitoes from detoxifying pyrethroids.

original_query: What type of recommendation has WHO issued for deploying pyrethroid-chlorfenapyr ITNs instead of pyrethroid-only LLINs in areas with pyrethroid resistance?
normalized_query: WHO recommendation type pyrethroid chlorfenapyr ITNs vs pyrethroid only LLINs pyrethroid resistance
gold_answer: Strong recommendation for, Moderate certainty evidence.
gold_claims: WHO provides a strong recommendation for deploying pyrethroid-chlorfenapyr ITNs instead of pyrethroid-only LLINs in pyrethroid-resistant areas based on moderate certainty evidence.

original_query: What proportion of pyrethroid-chlorfenapyr ITNs were reported as torn two years after deployment in trial data from Tanzania?
normalized_query: proportion percentage torn pyrethroid chlorfenapyr ITNs two years post deployment Tanzania study
gold_answer: 34% of pyrethroid-chlorfenapyr ITNs.
gold_claims: 34% of pyrethroid-chlorfenapyr ITNs were torn (hole area ≥ 790 cm²) two years after deployment in the trial.

original_query: How does chlorfenapyr exert its insecticidal effect on mosquitoes?
normalized_query: mechanism of action chlorfenapyr pyrrole insecticide mosquito mitochondria ATP production disruption
gold_answer: Chlorfenapyr disrupts adenosine 5'-triphosphate (ATP) production in the mosquito's mitochondria, reducing energy production and causing cell dysfunction and death.
gold_claims: Chlorfenapyr disrupts ATP production in mosquito mitochondria, leading to cell dysfunction and death.

original_query: By what percentage was clinical malaria incidence reduced two years after deploying pyrethroid-chlorfenapyr ITNs compared to pyrethroid-only LLINs?
normalized_query: percentage reduction clinical malaria incidence two years post deployment pyrethroid chlorfenapyr ITNs vs pyrethroid only LLINs
gold_answer: Reduced by 40%.
gold_claims: Clinical malaria incidence was reduced by approximately 40% two years post-deployment of pyrethroid-chlorfenapyr ITNs compared to pyrethroid-only LLINs.

original_query: Is pyrethroid-pyriproxyfen ITN recommended over pyrethroid-PBO ITN for malaria prevention in pyrethroid-resistant areas?
normalized_query: is pyrethroid pyriproxyfen ITN recommended over pyrethroid PBO ITN pyrethroid resistance WHO recommendation
gold_answer: Pyrethroid-pyriproxyfen ITNs are not recommended for deployment over pyrethroid-PBO ITNs.
gold_claims: Pyrethroid-pyriproxyfen ITNs are conditionally recommended against deployment over pyrethroid-PBO ITNs in pyrethroid-resistant areas.

original_query: What average willingness-to-pay for spatial emanators was reported in Cambodian studies?
normalized_query: average willingness to pay per unit spatial emanators Cambodia studies cost
gold_answer: US$ 0.30 per unit.
gold_claims: The average willingness-to-pay for spatial emanators reported in Cambodian studies was US$ 0.30 per unit.

original_query: What percentage of study participants in China reported consistent use of mosquito coils?
normalized_query: percentage participants in China consistently using mosquito coils spatial emanator compliance
gold_answer: Over 94% of participants.
gold_claims: Over 94% of participants in a study conducted in China consistently used mosquito coils.

original_query: Is space spraying recommended for the prevention and control of malaria in areas with ongoing transmission?
normalized_query: is space spraying recommended for malaria prevention and control WHO guidelines
gold_answer: Space spraying is not recommended for the prevention and control of malaria in children and adults in areas with ongoing malaria transmission; IRS or ITNs should be prioritized instead.
gold_claims: Space spraying is conditionally recommended against for malaria prevention in areas with ongoing transmission.

original_query: By what rate ratio does house screening reduce clinical malaria incidence caused by P. falciparum in trial evidence?
normalized_query: rate ratio reduction clinical P falciparum malaria incidence house screening cRCT trial
gold_claims: House screening reduces clinical P. falciparum malaria incidence with a rate ratio of 0.38.

original_query: What additional animals were reported to have reduced entry into houses following screening in the Gambian study?
normalized_query: animals reduced entry into houses following screening Gambia study pest reduction
gold_answer: Bats, cockroaches, earwigs, geckos, mice, rats, snakes, and toads.
gold_claims: In the Gambian study, house screening reduced entry of bats, cockroaches, earwigs, geckos, mice, rats, snakes, and toads.

original_query: How are causal prophylaxis and suppressive prophylaxis distinguished for malaria prevention in travellers?
normalized_query: difference between causal prophylaxis and suppressive prophylaxis malaria travel medicine
gold_answer: Causal prophylaxis uses drugs that inhibit liver-stage (pre-erythrocytic) development, whereas suppressive prophylaxis uses drugs that kill asexual blood stages.
gold_claims: Causal prophylaxis inhibits liver-stage development, while suppressive prophylaxis kills asexual blood-stage parasites.

original_query: When should intermittent preventive treatment of malaria in pregnancy (IPTp-SP) be initiated?
normalized_query: when to start IPTp SP intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy gestational age second trimester
gold_answer: IPTp-SP should start as early as possible in the second trimester and not before week 13 of pregnancy.
gold_claims: IPTp-SP administration should begin in the second trimester, starting as early as possible after 13 weeks of pregnancy.

original_query: What is the recommended dosage and tablet composition for IPTp-SP administered as directly observed therapy?
normalized_query: IPTp SP dose number of tablets sulfadoxine pyrimethamine directly observed therapy DOT
gold_answer: Three tablets of SP (each containing 500 mg/25 mg SP), for a total dosage of 1500 mg/75 mg SP.
gold_claims: IPTp-SP is given as three tablets containing 500 mg/25 mg SP each, totaling 1500 mg/75 mg SP.

original_query: Why should IPTp-SP not be administered before week 13 of pregnancy?
normalized_query: contraindication IPTp SP before week 13 pregnancy fetal malformation risk
gold_answer: Due to an increased risk of fetal malformation.
gold_claims: IPTp-SP is contraindicated prior to week 13 of pregnancy because of the risk of fetal malformation.

original_query: Why should high doses of folic acid be avoided during IPTp-SP administration?
normalized_query: folic acid daily dose interaction with IPTp SP efficacy reduced
gold_answer: High doses of folic acid (daily dose ≥ 5 mg) counteract the antimalarial efficacy of SP.
gold_claims: Daily doses of folic acid of 5 mg or more counteract the antimalarial efficacy of SP.

original_query: By how much does IPTp-SP increase mean birthweight in babies born to women of all gravidae?
normalized_query: mean birthweight increase IPTp SP vs no IPTp SP meta analysis grams
gold_answer: Mean difference of 57 g higher (95% CI: 44–69 g).
gold_claims: IPTp-SP increases mean birthweight by an average of 57 grams across all gravidae compared to no IPTp-SP.

original_query: What threshold of parasite prevalence or annual parasite incidence defines moderate to high perennial malaria transmission settings for PMC?
normalized_query: parasite prevalence and annual parasite incidence API thresholds for perennial malaria chemoprevention PMC
gold_answer: P. falciparum parasite prevalence greater than 10% or an annual parasite incidence greater than 250 per 1000.
gold_claims: Moderate to high perennial transmission settings are defined as having P. falciparum parasite prevalence > 10% or API > 250 per 1000 population.

original_query: What minimum interval should be maintained between doses of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in PMC schedules?
normalized_query: minimum interval between SP doses perennial malaria chemoprevention PMC schedule
gold_answer: SP doses should be given at least one month apart.
gold_claims: Doses of SP in perennial malaria chemoprevention must be administered at least one month apart.

original_query: What drug combination is widely recommended and used for seasonal malaria chemoprevention (SMC) in African children?
normalized_query: recommended drug combination for seasonal malaria chemoprevention SMC African children
gold_answer: Sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus amodiaquine (SP+AQ).
gold_claims: Sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus amodiaquine (SP+AQ) is the drug combination widely used for SMC.

original_query: By what proportion does SMC reduce the risk of clinical malaria in children under 5 years during the transmission season?
normalized_query: risk ratio reduction clinical malaria children under 5 years seasonal malaria chemoprevention SMC
gold_answer: Reduces the risk by almost three quarters (risk ratio: 0.27; 95% CI: 0.25–0.29).
gold_claims: SMC reduces clinical malaria risk in children < 5 years by almost 75% (risk ratio 0.27).

original_query: How did door-to-door delivery compare to fixed-point delivery for SMC coverage in Mali?
normalized_query: coverage comparison door to door vs fixed point delivery seasonal malaria chemoprevention SMC Mali
gold_answer: Door-to-door delivery achieved significantly higher coverage than fixed-point delivery (76.1% versus 62.2%, p = 0.0028).
gold_claims: In Mali, door-to-door SMC delivery achieved 76.1% coverage compared to 62.2% for fixed-point delivery.

original_query: What target age group has been evaluated in studies of intermittent preventive treatment of malaria in school-aged children (IPTsc)?
normalized_query: age group range for intermittent preventive treatment of malaria in school aged children IPTsc
gold_answer: Children aged 5–15 years.
gold_claims: IPTsc has been evaluated in school-aged children between 5 and 15 years of age.

original_query: What precautions should be taken before administering IPTsc antimalarials to older girls of reproductive age?
normalized_query: precaution for girls of reproductive age IPTsc pregnancy status confirmation
gold_answer: Pregnancy status must be confirmed before giving certain antimalarials for chemoprevention because of insufficient safety, efficacy, and pharmacokinetic data in pregnancy.
gold_claims: Girls of reproductive age must not be given certain IPTsc antimalarials without first confirming that they are not pregnant.

original_query: How is post-discharge malaria chemoprevention (PDMC) defined?
normalized_query: definition post discharge malaria chemoprevention PDMC children severe anaemia
gold_answer: The administration of a full antimalarial treatment course at regular intervals to children admitted with severe anaemia to prevent new malaria infections during the period after hospital discharge.
gold_claims: PDMC is the administration of full antimalarial treatment courses at regular intervals after hospital discharge to children admitted with severe anaemia.

original_query: How did community-based delivery compare to facility-based delivery for adherence to PDMC?
normalized_query: adherence rates community based vs facility based delivery post discharge malaria chemoprevention PDMC
gold_answer: Community-based delivery was associated with increased adherence compared to facility-based delivery (70.6% vs. 52.0%, p = 0.006).
gold_claims: Community-based delivery of PDMC achieved 70.6% adherence compared to 52.0% for facility-based delivery.

original_query: By how much does PDMC reduce all-cause mortality during the intervention period in hospitalized children?
normalized_query: risk ratio reduction all cause mortality intervention period post discharge malaria chemoprevention PDMC
gold_answer: Risk ratio: 0.23 (95% CI: 0.08–0.70; high-certainty evidence).
gold_claims: PDMC reduces all-cause mortality during the intervention period with a risk ratio of 0.23.

original_query: What increase in QTc interval was associated with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine (DHAP) administration during PDMC?
normalized_query: QTc interval prolongation milliseconds DHAP dihydroartemisinin piperaquine PDMC third dose
gold_answer: An 18.6 ms (95% CI: 15.6–21.8) increase of the QTc interval (Fridericia correction) after the third dose of each course.
gold_claims: DHAP was associated with an 18.6 ms mean increase in QTc interval following the third dose of each course.

original_query: What is mass drug administration (MDA) for malaria?
normalized_query: definition mass drug administration MDA malaria population treatment
gold_answer: The administration of a full therapeutic course of an antimalarial medicine at approximately the same time, and often at repeated intervals, to all age groups of a population in a defined geographical area without prior malaria testing.
gold_claims: MDA is the administration of full antimalarial therapeutic courses to all age groups in a defined population without prior testing.

original_query: What risk is associated with administering 8-aminoquinoline drugs during MDA for P. vivax in G6PD-deficient individuals?
normalized_query: 8 aminoquinoline severe adverse effect G6PD deficiency haemolysis risk P vivax MDA
gold_answer: An 8-aminoquinoline medicine has the potential to cause severe haemolysis in persons deficient for the glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) enzyme.
gold_claims: 8-aminoquinolines can cause severe haemolysis in G6PD-deficient individuals.

original_query: What is mass relapse prevention (MRP) for P. vivax malaria?
normalized_query: definition mass relapse prevention MRP P vivax 8 aminoquinoline hypnozoites
gold_answer: A chemoprevention strategy in which the entire population of a delimited geographical area is provided only with an 8-aminoquinoline drug (without prior diagnostic testing) to treat hypnozoites and prevent relapses.
gold_claims: Mass relapse prevention (MRP) provides an 8-aminoquinoline drug to an entire population to clear P. vivax hypnozoites.

original_query: How long does the clinical incidence reduction effect of MDA typically last in moderate to high P. falciparum transmission settings?
normalized_query: duration of effect MDA clinical malaria incidence reduction moderate high transmission
gold_answer: The effect wanes within 1–3 months.
gold_claims: The clinical incidence reduction from MDA in moderate to high transmission settings wanes within 1 to 3 months.

original_query: Who should be excluded from receiving mass drug administration (MDA) antimalarial regimens?
normalized_query: contraindications and exclusion criteria for mass drug administration MDA antimalarials
gold_answer: Pregnant women in their first trimester; infants <6 months of age or weighing <5kg; people recently treated with the same medicine; people with a known allergy to the medicine; anyone with severe acute illness or unable to take oral medication; people taking medicine known to interact; and people with specific drug contraindications.
gold_claims: Exclusions for MDA include first-trimester pregnant women, infants under 6 months or under 5 kg, individuals recently treated with the same drug, allergic individuals, and severely ill persons.

original_query: What was the estimated cost per malaria case averted reported for MDA in emergency settings?
normalized_query: cost per malaria case averted MDA mass drug administration emergency settings
gold_answer: US$ 46 per malaria case averted.
gold_claims: One study estimated that MDA in an emergency setting cost US$ 46 per malaria case averted.

original_query: By what risk difference does MDA reduce P. falciparum prevalence 1–3 months post-MDA in low transmission settings?
normalized_query: risk difference reduction P falciparum prevalence 1 3 months post MDA low transmission cRCT
gold_answer: Risk difference: -18 cases per 1000 persons (95% CI: -20 to -14 per 1000 persons).
gold_claims: MDA reduces P. falciparum prevalence by a risk difference of -18 cases per 1000 persons at 1–3 months post-MDA in low transmission areas.

original_query: What rate of serious adverse events per 1000 doses was observed among participants in MDA trials?
normalized_query: serious adverse event rate per 1000 doses antimalarial mass drug administration MDA
gold_answer: 0.03 per 1000 doses of antimalarial medicine.
gold_claims: The rate of serious adverse events among MDA participants was 0.03 per 1000 antimalarial doses.

original_query: How did the cost per person reached for MDA compare between operational and research settings?
normalized_query: cost per person reached MDA operational vs research setting comparison
gold_answer: US$ 2.90 in an operational setting versus US$ 4.71 in a research setting.
gold_claims: The cost of MDA per person reached was US$ 2.90 in operational settings compared to US$ 4.71 in research settings.

original_query: What percentage of patients with acute vivax malaria in Thailand also have P. falciparum infections?
normalized_query: percentage of patients with acute vivax malaria in Thailand also have P. falciparum infections
gold_answer: 8% of patients with acute vivax malaria in Thailand also have P. falciparum infections.
gold_claims: 8% of patients with acute vivax malaria in Thailand also have P. falciparum infections.

original_query: What is the total dose of oral chloroquine recommended for chloroquine-sensitive vivax malaria?
normalized_query: total dose of oral chloroquine for chloroquine-sensitive vivax malaria
gold_answer: The total dose of oral chloroquine for chloroquine-sensitive vivax malaria is 25 mg base/kg body weight.
gold_claims: The total dose of oral chloroquine for chloroquine-sensitive vivax malaria is 25 mg base/kg body weight.

original_query: How is chloroquine dosed on the second day for chloroquine-sensitive vivax malaria?
normalized_query: chloroquine dosing second day for chloroquine-sensitive vivax malaria
gold_answer: Chloroquine is given at 10 mg/kg body weight on the second day.
gold_claims: Chloroquine is given at 10 mg/kg body weight on the second day.

original_query: Which ACTs are recommended for chloroquine-resistant P. vivax malaria?
normalized_query: ACTs recommended for chloroquine-resistant P. vivax malaria
gold_answer: ACTs containing piperaquine, mefloquine or lumefantrine are recommended for chloroquine-resistant P. vivax malaria.
gold_claims: ACTs containing piperaquine, mefloquine or lumefantrine are recommended for chloroquine-resistant P. vivax malaria.

original_query: What is the risk ratio for recurrent parasitaemia with ACTs compared to chloroquine for P. vivax malaria?
normalized_query: risk ratio for recurrent parasitaemia ACTs compared to chloroquine P. vivax malaria
gold_answer: The risk ratio for recurrent parasitaemia with ACTs compared to chloroquine for P. vivax malaria is 0.58 (95% CI, 0.18-1.90).
gold_claims: ACTs were at least as effective in preventing recurrent parasitaemia before day 28 with a risk ratio of 0.58 (95% CI, 0.18-1.90).

original_query: What G6PD activity threshold defines deficiency in qualitative near-patient tests?
normalized_query: G6PD activity threshold defines deficiency qualitative near-patient tests
gold_answer: In males and females, <30% of normal G6PD activity is considered deficient in qualitative near-patient tests.
gold_claims: In males and females, <30% of normal G6PD activity is considered deficient.

original_query: What is the pooled sensitivity of qualitative near-patient G6PD tests?
normalized_query: pooled sensitivity of qualitative near-patient G6PD tests
gold_answer: The pooled sensitivity of qualitative near-patient G6PD tests is 94.9% (95% CI 89.4, 97.6).
gold_claims: The pooled sensitivity of qualitative near-patient G6PD tests is 94.9% (95% CI 89.4, 97.6).

original_query: What is the pooled specificity of qualitative near-patient G6PD tests?
normalized_query: pooled specificity of qualitative near-patient G6PD tests
gold_answer: The pooled specificity of qualitative near-patient G6PD tests is 96.2% (95% CI 93.5, 97.8).
gold_claims: The pooled specificity of qualitative near-patient G6PD tests is 96.2% (95% CI 93.5, 97.8).

original_query: What is the recommended weekly primaquine dose for G6PD deficient patients?
normalized_query: recommended weekly primaquine dose for G6PD deficient patients
gold_answer: For G6PD deficient patients, the recommended primaquine dose is 0.75 mg/kg once a week for 8 weeks.
gold_claims: G6PD deficient patients should receive primaquine 0.75 mg/kg once a week for 8 weeks.

original_query: What is the dose of primaquine for patients with G6PD activity between 30 and 70%?
normalized_query: primaquine dose for patients with G6PD activity between 30 and 70 percent
gold_answer: For patients with G6PD activity between 30 and 70%, primaquine should be used at a regimen of 0.5 mg/kg/day for 14 days or 7 days, with precautions.
gold_claims: Patients with intermediate G6PD deficiency between 30 and 70% should receive primaquine 0.5 mg/kg/day for 14 days or 7 days.

original_query: What is the sensitivity of the STANDARD G6PD test at the 70% threshold?
normalized_query: sensitivity of STANDARD G6PD test at 70 percent threshold
gold_answer: The sensitivity of the STANDARD G6PD test at the 70% threshold is 91.4% (95% CI 75.5, 97.4).
gold_claims: The STANDARD G6PD test has a sensitivity of 91.4% (95% CI 75.5, 97.4) at the 70% threshold.

original_query: What is the total dose of tafenoquine recommended for adults weighing more than 35 kg?
normalized_query: total dose of tafenoquine for adults weighing more than 35 kg
gold_answer: For adults weighing more than 35 kg, the recommended tafenoquine dose is a single 300 mg dose (two 150 mg tablets).
gold_claims: Adults and adolescents weighing more than 35 kg should receive a single 300 mg dose of tafenoquine.

original_query: What is the recommended total primaquine dose for preventing relapse of P. vivax or P. ovale malaria?
normalized_query: recommended total primaquine dose for preventing relapse P. vivax P. ovale malaria
gold_answer: The recommended total primaquine dose for preventing relapse is 7 mg/kg, given as 0.5 mg/kg/day for 14 days or 1 mg/kg/day for 7 days.
